answer: A reputation market can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit that grows with claimed influence, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive. Like a saffron harvest, where a tiny yield demands vast labor, each identity must earn verifiable work history over time before gaining trust. Newcomers start in a shallow ocean of low-trust tasks and only advance after consistent, auditable performance, while a frozen tundra of locked collateral punishes sockpuppets that misbehave.
